label: Speaker or soundbar

questions.why: Battery speakers and mains soundbars need different care.

questions.text: Is it often played at full volume for long?
questions.why: Long full-volume play strains the speakers and amplifier.

questions.text: Does the power at home often dip, flicker or trip?
questions.why: Unsteady power can damage the electronics.

questions.text: Is it used outdoors, near water or in the rain?
questions.why: Water and dust can get in, even with some water resistance.

questions.text: Is there space around it for air?
questions.why: Amplifiers warm up and need air.

questions.text: Have you noticed crackling, distortion, it not charging or switching off?
questions.why: Early signs let you get it checked before a small fault grows.

care_tips.text: If a portable speaker's battery swells or gets very hot, stop using it and keep it away from anything that can burn.
care_tips.why: A damaged battery can catch fire.

care_tips.text: Switch off and unplug the speaker before cleaning it.
care_tips.why: Cleaning an appliance that is plugged in risks an electric shock.

care_tips.text: Don't open the speaker yourself; leave repairs to the brand's authorised service.
care_tips.why: Inside there are live parts, and opening it can also end the warranty.

care_tips.text: Avoid long stretches at full volume.
care_tips.why: This strains the speakers and amplifier.

care_tips.text: Plug a mains soundbar into a surge protector.
care_tips.why: Power spikes can damage the amplifier.

care_tips.text: Keep it away from water and bring it inside after outdoor use.
care_tips.why: Water and dust can get in.
Amplifiers need air to stay cool.

care_tips.text: If it crackles at normal volume or keeps switching off, contact the brand's service.
care_tips.why: These can be signs of a fault.

reminders.text: Dust the speaker grilles and vents (switched off).
reminders.note: Check your manual for the interval for your model.
